title: Finite-round comparison: quantifier rank and Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé games
summary: Compare structures using a fixed number of choices, and prove that the resulting game captures formulas with a fixed quantifier depth.
abstract: How much of a structure can a formula see when it can nest only a few quantifiers? A finite game turns this question into a sequence of choices: one player selects points, while the other tries to match them without changing any equality or relation among the selected points. We prove that surviving a fixed number of rounds is exactly what it takes to preserve all formulas of that quantifier depth, provided the language has only finitely many relation symbols. The proof builds finite descriptions of all the patterns that matter at each depth. Examples in the language of equality show how many fresh points a formula can detect, while an infinite family of predicates explains why the restriction on the language matters.
